explanation: NearBlocks documents neither count, but the numbers show what each one is. v1 matches Nansen's published distinct signers, and v3 stays within 2% of v1 plus meta_accounts, so it also counts users whose transactions a relayer signs. metric: Mean daily active contracts over 30 days
NEAR burned on the days before issuance began
source_b: Fall in total supply on the same days
explanation: Expected: burn_near is a lower bound, and this is the one place it can be measured. Before issuance began on 2020-10-20 nothing was minted, so every fall in total supply was gas burned. Over those 79 days supply fell by 124.4 NEAR against gas fees of 146.8 NEAR, which is 84.8% of gas, while burn_near takes 70%. The contracts' share was 30% of the gas burnt executing function calls, not of all gas, so the real burn was always more than 70% of the fee and never more than all of it (fct_chain_daily.gas_fee_near). The lower bound held on every one of the 79 days, which the data test burn_is_a_lower_bound_before_issuance keeps. The 84.8% belongs to 2020's mix of transactions, so it is not applied to later years; treat burn_near before 2026-11-04 as a floor. From that day protocol version 87 burns all gas and the column is exact.

explanation: Open question. DefiLlama matches wallet transfers within 0.1%, and the page's own wallet table matches them within 0.3%, but the page's monthly series totals about 697k NEAR and $1.71M more. About 141k NEAR of that falls in Aug to Oct 2025, before the wallets received anything; most later months add more. NEAR does not publish how this series is built, so it may count revenue when accrued rather than when swept. Treat the wallet-based figure as the checkable one.

DefiLlama's Intents volume changes meaning on 2026-09-01. From 2026-04-01 to 2026-08-31 it matches NearBlocks' public-only figure within 0.2% (see intents_volume_2026_apr_aug_defillama_vs_nearblocks), and from 2026-09-01 it equals revenue.near.org's all-routes figure, which includes confidential Intents. Its adapter carries no date rule, so the likely cause is that DefiLlama kept its stored daily values when NEAR restated the earlier months; that is not confirmed. So gold's fct_intents_daily takes all-route volume from revenue.near.org (volume_usd) and public volume from NearBlocks (public_volume_usd), and keeps DefiLlama's series only here. Its fees change scope the same way, through 2026-09-13.
